claims.text: Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 has a high-temperature BCC state.
Annealing just below the high-temperature BCC stability range promotes local solute partitioning.
Local solute partitioning creates nucleation sites for secondary-phase precipitation during subsequent water quenching.
The annealing-and-quenching process produces a mixed-phase microstructure.
The resulting mixed-phase microstructure depends on annealing temperature and duration.
Sub-critical annealing permits diffusion that creates localized compositional inhomogeneities.
Localized compositional inhomogeneities serve as nucleation sites for phases that depart from the original BCC structure during rapid cooling.
Relative diffusion rates and solute-partitioning dynamics established during annealing govern the resulting phase mixture.
Immediate water quenching from the high-temperature BCC state preserves a primarily uniform BCC structure with minimal secondary-phase formation.
Relative to immediate quenching, annealing just below the BCC stability range followed by quenching increases the volume fraction of non-BCC secondary phases.
The secondary phases will exhibit distinct morphologies and phase boundaries influenced by local solute segregation.
The proposed mechanism applies only within a narrow annealing temperature-and-time window that permits measurable partitioning without complete transformation.
Annealing too far below the BCC stability range yields insufficient diffusion for the proposed mechanism.
Excessive annealing can eliminate the predicted response by producing homogenization or a complete transformation.
Additional thermomechanical deformation places the alloy outside the stated applicability of the mechanism.
